result.summary: Wrote r3/lit.md covering the 4 literature topics (L1-L4) from r3/analysis.md's §5, aimed at core A (day_distinct_ratio(Volume) minute-level illiquidity), N-alpha (descaled realized vol-of-vol), F3's rolling-beta methodology, and N-beta (end-of-day volume share). All sources restricted to pre-2023-08-08 publications. Highlight: directly read Frazzini-Pedersen (2014) "Betting Against Beta" full text, confirming beta=corr*vol_ratio decomposition with asymmetric windows and mandatory Vasicek(1973) shrinkage toward 1 -- none of which the 24 F3 heads do -- plus Dimson(1979)/Scholes-Williams(1977) on sparse-trading bias and Chordia-Roll-Subrahmanyam(2000) on what a literature-standard "liquidity beta" actually regresses. For L2, established that Baltussen et al. (2018)'s benchmark vol-of-vol construction is itself unscaled (on implied vol), so the coefficient-of-variation descaling step is our own adaptation, not literature replication -- confirming the plausibility cap at 4 not 5, and confirming a genuine search gap for realized-vol-based vol-of-vol. For L4, found two new direct DID studies of the exact 2018-08-20 Shanghai closing-auction reform (Han et al. 2022 PBFJ; Ma et al. 2020 CFRI) plus a verifiable SSE research-center report (Shi Donghui 2006), upgrading what r2/lit.md could only cite as a regulatory announcement. 22 references listed with full citation + verified:true/false flags; honest gaps recorded (e.g. Bogousslavsky-Muravyev "Who Trades at the Close?" excluded for unverifiable date; an unverifiable 1997-2005 A-share liquidity-premium thesis excluded, 403 error on source).
